title: The Endurance Passes Saturn
testing: Whether the proven 3-star shape (named parts, one soft distant pulse, a sung hook, a bloom past the middle) still lands with a church pipe organ as the lead voice instead of the lyre/duduk/dulcimer folk palette.
prompt: Warm cinematic ambient in A Lydian at ~60 BPM, hushed and full of awe — Interstellar, the Endurance coasting past Saturn, the crew at the window as the rings slide by, the wormhole waiting ahead and everyone still hopeful. THE SHIP: a vast church pipe organ holds a steady low A pedal with soft tremulant, the air of the pipes audible, while very quiet diegetic life fills the hull — the faint hum of air handlers, slow metal ticks of the rotating ring cooling, a distant beacon pulse once every few seconds like an easy heartbeat far back in the mix, and soft breath on an open radio channel. THE RINGS: the hook — the organ's upper manual plays a simple four-note rising figure that lifts and settles back, patient and wondering, answered after each pass by warm bowed cello and a soft glass harmonica shimmer, as if light were moving across ice. THE DISTANCE: swelling French horns and warm string pads voice a slow I–II–IV–I pendulum (A — B — D — A) with added 9ths and gentle sus4 suspensions over the unbroken tonic pedal, with an airy granular wash of vacuum and starlight floating above. Opens with the organ pedal, beacon pulse and hull hum alone; the four-note figure enters by itself, then cello and horns gradually gather like the planet filling the window; past the midpoint the music becomes CLOSER and WARMER, never louder or harsher, the hook doubled by horns and shimmer at its fullest; the last stretch eases into a calm lit glow while every instrument keeps sounding at full presence — organ, cellos, horns, glass and beacon all sustaining through the final seconds, no fade-out, no silence, the ship still under way as it ends. Richly textured yet spacious, instrumental, reverent and hopeful, never busy, always moving forward. No cymbals or crash percussion of any kind, no drum kit, no electric guitar. Nothing ominous or dissonant — the organ is warm cathedral light, not dread. Hull sounds and the beacon stay soft and distant.

title: Frodo Sails West
testing: Whether the 3-star sea-voyage shape works in a new world (The Lord of the Rings), with a wordless female voice as the hook in a hopeful scene. The only sung hook he has rated before was in the perilous Sirens take. (Panel winner; judge fixes applied: less grief, no gulls, voice kept distant.)
prompt: Warm cinematic ambient in D major at ~56 BPM, full of hope and gratitude. The Lord of the Rings, the very end: Frodo boards the white ship with Gandalf and Bilbo and sails into the West, and far out at sea Frodo sees the grey veil turn to silver glass and roll back on white shores and a far green country under a swift sunrise. THE SHIP: a soft frame drum pulses like a slow, easy heartbeat far back in the mix, with very quiet creaks of rope and timber, the hush of the bow through calm water, and a sail filling. THE FAREWELL: the hook, a soft, distant wordless female voice sings a slow four-note call (never operatic, never in front of the mix), rising from D up a fourth to G, a step higher to A, then settling back on G, tender and unhurried, answered each time by a Celtic harp rippling slow open arpeggios and a breathy low whistle. THE FAR GREEN COUNTRY: warm cellos, string pads and swelling French horns voice a slow I-vi-IV-I progression (D, Bm, G, D) with added 9ths and gentle sus2 suspensions over a steady tonic D pedal, with soft glass shimmer like light on water floating above. Opens in a silver-grey haze with the pedal, the heartbeat, the harp and the sea; the voice enters alone, far off; cellos and horns gradually gather as the haze parts and the light turns from silver to gold; past the midpoint the music is fullest, CLOSER and WARMER rather than louder, the call doubled by low whistle and horns as the far shore comes into view; the last stretch settles into a calm sunrise glow while every instrument keeps sounding at full presence through the final seconds, no fade-out, no silence, the ship still sailing on as it ends. Richly textured yet spacious, instrumental except the wordless voice, grateful and hopeful, a farewell without grief, always moving forward. No cymbals or crash percussion, no drum kit, no electric guitar. The sea stays soft and distant.

title: Fair Wind Home, With a Voice
testing: Whether adding a soft, distant wordless female voice as the hook to the 3-star Fair Wind take keeps it at 3 stars. This separates the voice from the new world in the 2-star Frodo Sails West.
prompt: Warm cinematic ambient soundscape in D Mixolydian at ~64 BPM — Aeolus' fair wind carrying the ship home at golden hour, hopeful and expansive. THE WIND: airy sustained pads and glass shimmer with a soft granular wash of wind filling a full sail, always moving forward. THE SHIP: a distant frame drum pulses like an easy heartbeat beneath quiet rope and hull creaks and waves lapping past the bow — the crew at ease, the sea friendly at last. HOME AHEAD: French horn swells and warm cello pads voice a slow I–bVII–IV–I pendulum with added 9ths and gentle sus4 suspensions over a steady tonic pedal, while a soft, distant wordless female voice sings the hook, a slow three-note call falling gently from A to F-sharp and settling on D, tender and unhurried, never operatic, never in front of the mix, answered each time by an ancient lyre tracing slow yearning figures far back in the mix and a soft wooden flute breathing warm phrases — the sound of a horizon that finally holds Ithaca. Opens with wind, heartbeat pulse and pedal; strings, horns and shimmer gradually fill like the day turning gold; at its fullest the music becomes CLOSER and WARMER, never louder or harsher; the final quarter eases into a calm sunlit glow while every instrument sustains at full presence through the very last seconds — no fade-out, no silence, the voyage still under way as it ends. Richly textured yet unhurried, never busy, instrumental except the wordless voice, breathing with homeward hope through the very end.
